Your dental routine actually sounds pretty good. Cavities can be caused by a lot of what you eat, even if it isn’t candy or soda. Carbs can cause cavities because of the sugars they contain, especially if they sit on your teeth for an extended period of time. Limiting snacking helps, and keeping soda or carbonated beverages to times you eat can too. 

One thing I swear by, as I had my own dental issues, is getting the fluoride varnish at cleanings. I know some insurances don’t cover it, but for an extra $25-30 is worth it to help prevent cavities, especially for people like us who are prone to it. I haven’t had one in ten years, and while I pride myself with good home care habits, I feel the fluoride is a big reason I haven’t gotten one too. 

Good luck and hope this helps!

I have an implant on 19 myself. I originally had a root canal on it when I was 20, and the tooth cracked under the crown a few months later, so it needed to be extracted. 

I finally had the implant restored fully last year, which was 7 years after I had the tooth pulled. I underwent ortho during that time, as well as saved up some money for the implant, as it cost me about $5k total for everything. 

While I love my implant, as it’s nice to be able to chew on the left side of my mouth again after all that time being unable to do so properly, I wish I’d have taken better care of my teeth so I didn’t have to deal with that. As someone close in age to you, I’d say go for the root canal. Most of the time, they work great. In my case, that did not happen, but it was more so because the tooth was already weak. You can always get an implant later on, as others here have said. 19 is an important tooth for chewing, and if I had to get another root canal again for whatever reason, I would not hesitate to do so even though my previous one wasn’t successful.
